fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Detached Structure; Walkway
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Multiple Access Points; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker visible from the road at the driveway entrance.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly so responders can distinguish it from other openings along the road frontage.
• Post structure identification markers on both the main residence and detached structures so responders can quickly locate and distinguish each building.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles from ground level to a height that allows truck passage.
• Clear vegetation crowding the walkways connecting structures so responders can move between buildings without obstruction.
• Keep all gates providing rear access unlocked or fitted with a rapid-access lock compatible with local fire department tools.
• Mark any secondary access points to the rear of the property so responders arriving under low-visibility conditions can locate them quickly.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of stored items so responders can use it as a staging area.
• Thin dense vegetation between the detached structures and the main residence so responders have a clear path between buildings.
• Post a simple site map near the driveway entrance showing the location of all structures and access points on the property.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Brush Area; Grass Cover; Open Terrain; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Scattered Shrubs; Multiple Access Routes; Vegetation Near Structure
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs and low branches that are directly touching or within a few feet of the structure.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to increase open space between the canopy and the building.
• Cut grass around the structure short, particularly in the area between the building and surrounding brush.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from shrubs growing close to the structure.
• Clear any brush that has grown toward the structure from the surrounding brush area.
• Keep low tree branches trimmed up from the ground near the structure to reduce the chance of fire climbing into the canopy.
• Maintain open ground between the scattered shrubs and the structure so fire moving through the grass has less to carry it forward.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so vehicles can move through without obstruction.
